newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr off highs against yen, mark by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr off highs against yen, mark by late Tokyo.

text.p: 0626 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar was off its highs against the yen and the mark by late afternoon Tokyo on Tuesday, with Tokyo operators awaiting the release of Japan's current account data for April on Wednesday.
The dollar erased earlier losses versus the yen by noon after Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka called recent forex movements excessive.
Mitsuzuka also said Japan will deal appropriately with excessive currency moves.
After Mitsuzuka's remarks, the dollar briefly rebounded above 113 yen on buy-back interest by overseas speculative funds, as well as buying by Japanese institutional investors.
However, the dollar was capped by hedge-selling interest from Japanese trust banks and exporters above 113 yen, dealers said.
"For now, 113 yen is looking quite heavy. We could test yesterday's low again if tomorrow's current account number offers a surprise," said a city bank trader.
Japan's current account surplus, due at 8.50 a.m. on Wednesday (2350 GMT on Tuesday), is widely expected to increase substantially from the year-ago period.

A Reuters poll of economists showed, on average, that the April current account surplus would grow to 1.13 trillion yen, compared with a surplus of 566.6 billion yen last year. The forecasts ranged from 990 billion yen to 1.21 trillion yen.
Some dealers said a bigger-than-expected surplus could push the dollar back below 112 yen.
The dollar fell as low as 111.80 yen in Tokyo on Monday, its lowest level since November 25, 1996.
"I think the dollar/yen's downside risk will remain ahead of the Denver summit, because concerns about Japan's trade surplus will not go away so soon," said a trust bank trader.
The Group of Seven (G7) leaders will gather in Denver on June 20-22.
The dollar's rebound against the yen from earlier lows was partly helped by a large-lot sterling purchase for yen by a major local brokerage firm, dealers said.
A major Japanese brokerage house tapped the pound/yen market with 300 million sterling worth of bids in early trade, said a chief trader at a long-term bank.

Dealers said the large sterling bids were partly related to the launch of the 6.4 percent three-year straight eurobond worth 200 million pounds by Inter-American Development Bank on June 4. Payment is due on June 26.
Sterling stood at around 184.50/62 yen at 0727 GMT, up from around 184.14 yen earlier in the day. The mark was at around 65.96/99 yen, up from around 65.90 yen earlier.
Dealers expect the uncertainty about the future of the European economic and monetary union (EMU) to weigh on European currencies ahead of the European Union summit in Amsterdam on June 16-17.
French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Monday that the newly formed French government needed more time to study the bloc's stability pact.
Singapore dealers said the dollar's upside looked heavy against the yen and the mark. A European bank dealer said dollar/mark was bought from around the 1.7050 level by a U.S. fund in early trade.
The dollar closed at 112.90/00 yen and 1.7065/75 marks in New York on Monday.
